subject: CSEC Mathematics
question: Using π = 22/7, the area of the compound shape, in cm^2, is
stem: Using π = 22/7, the area of the compound shape, in cm^2, is

misconception.label: Found the rectangle only
misconception.remediation_hint: The semicircle on top must be added.

misconception.label: Added a whole circle instead of a semicircle
misconception.remediation_hint: Only half the circle sits on the rectangle, so halve that area.

misconception.label: Used the diameter as the radius
misconception.remediation_hint: The 14 cm side is the DIAMETER, so the radius is 7 cm.

worked_solution: Rectangle: 14 × 10 = 140 cm^2. Semicircle: radius = 14/2 = 7 cm, area = 1/2 × 22/7 × 7 × 7 = 77 cm^2. Total = 140 + 77 = 217 cm^2.
hints: The semicircle on top must be added.
Only half the circle sits on the rectangle, so halve that area.
The 14 cm side is the DIAMETER, so the radius is 7 cm.
common_mistakes: Added a whole circle instead of a semicircle
Used the diameter as the radius
learning_objective: Find the area of a compound shape.
exam_skill: Add the area of a rectangle to the area of a semicircle
